data.standardized_narrative: A small adverse prior-year reserve movement was identified (approximately 0.97 million, representing ~1.27% of opening gross claims outstanding), driven primarily by development on older (2017) underwriting years. The movement appears to be related to natural catastrophe experience in 2017 (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria) and adverse claims development/IBNR recalibration. No explicit prior-year gross movement figure is stated in narrative; the figure above is calculated from the syndicate's gross claims development table.
raw_causal_phrases: In 2017 the Atlantic Hurricane Season delivered three large Hurricanes, Harvey, Irma and Maria.
The year also saw Earthquakes in Mexico and extensive wildfires in California.
The main drivers for this loss were natural catastrophe losses suffered in second half of 2017 combined with further softening of rates across the portfolio.

The 2019 Year of account has unfortunately suffered a material loss from Typhoon Hagibis while following pricing reviews of the casualty account ultimate loss ratios have been reassessed upwards by Asta, which has been validated by Chord Re's approach to pricing the 2020 renewals.
The Syndicate is reliant on the accuracy of bordereau data provided by the AxaXL Group, which is another source of risk.
data.data_quality_notes: Primary financial statements prepared in USD. Some tables in the report are labelled with 'GBP ' but amounts reconcile to the USD-formatted statements; amounts reported here are in the report's functional currency (USD). No explicit gross 'movement in prior years' numeric statement was found; prior year development was derived from the gross claims development (cumulative) table by comparing the 2017 current estimate to its prior diagonal. exact_reserve_text is empty because no single sentence explicitly stated the gross prior-year movement. The prior year movement therefore has moderate confidence (0.8).
